claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a reported hierarchical heterostructure with multilevel chemical fluctuations.
A physics-informed surrogate can integrate atomistic fracture criteria with continuum-mechanics formulations.
A surrogate calibrated using a sparse set of high-fidelity DFT and fracture simulations can adequately represent the target alloy.
The proposed model can predict Young's modulus of hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10 with less than 5% error relative to experiment.
The proposed model can predict yield strength of hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10 with less than 5% error relative to experiment.
The proposed model can predict fracture toughness of hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10 with less than 5% error relative to experiment.
The proposed model will reduce computation time by approximately a factor of 10 relative to conventional CALPHAD, first-principles, machine-learning, or other high-fidelity approaches.
Explicitly encoding the hierarchical microstructure and multilevel chemical fluctuations will allow the surrogate to capture scale-bridging fracture behavior.
Embedding atomistic fracture mechanisms into a continuum-scale surrogate captures the multiscale effects governing elastic response.
Embedding atomistic fracture mechanisms into a continuum-scale surrogate captures the multiscale effects governing plastic response and yield strength.
Embedding atomistic fracture mechanisms into a continuum-scale surrogate captures the multiscale effects governing fracture toughness.
Conventional high-throughput CALPHAD calculations can involve massive numbers of calculations, making computational efficiency relevant to rapid HEA exploration.
Traditional DFT and standard machine-learning approaches are computationally expensive for this problem.
Existing CALPHAD, DFT, and standard machine-learning approaches often fail to capture fracture toughness reliably.
The model is expected to remain valid for tensile and fracture tests conducted at strain rates and temperatures within its calibration range.
The model may become unreliable at extreme strain rates, at temperatures outside its calibration range, after major microstructural changes, or during unforeseen phase transitions.
Accuracy and speedup will depend on how representative the high-fidelity calibration points are and whether all relevant multiscale phenomena are represented.
